boards.title: Your First Weekend at Princeton University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm, under-21-safe campus sequence that moves from orientation and history to art, gardens, and getting around Princeton.

cards.title: Start with a self-guided campus tour
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main campus
cards.notes: Use the smartphone self-guided tour to get oriented before choosing later stops; save a few landmarks for a second pass.
cards.short_summary: A flexible first walk through Princeton’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton Admission offers a self-guided campus tour via smartphone.
cards.access_notes: Use the self-guided tour on a smartphone; campus visitor policies apply.

cards.title: Stop at Nassau Hall
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main campus
cards.notes: Pause outside to take in the building’s scale, then use the University Archives history to connect it with Princeton’s early campus.
cards.short_summary: Princeton’s historic academic landmark anchors the opening walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Nassau Hall opened in 1756 and is a National Historic Landmark.
cards.source_title: A Brief History of the Architecture of Nassau Hall
cards.access_notes: View the exterior while following current campus visitor policy.

cards.title: Follow the Chapel audio tour
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Beside Firestone Library
cards.notes: Use the Chapel’s self-guided audio segments to look closely at its exterior, interior, and stained glass at your own pace.
cards.short_summary: A late-day architecture and audio-tour stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel offers a self-guided audio tour and is open daily from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are 7 a.m.–11 p.m.; people of all faiths are welcome for prayer and meditation.

cards.title: Make time for the Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Princeton University campus
cards.notes: Choose one gallery floor or exhibition rather than rushing the whole building, and check the visit page for the day’s hours.
cards.short_summary: A free museum stop with time to focus on a few works.
cards.evidence_claim: Princeton University Art Museum is free to all and posts daily visitor hours.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: Monday–Wednesday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Thursday–Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m.; Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sunday noon–5 p.m.

cards.title: Add the Milberg Gallery to your loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Firestone Library lobby
cards.notes: Look for the gallery in Firestone’s lobby and pair it with a short library stop; it is one of the public spaces available without an access card.
cards.short_summary: A public gallery inside Firestone Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Milberg Gallery in Firestone Library is open to the public without an access card during regular hours.
cards.access_notes: The gallery is open to the public during regular library hours; other Firestone spaces can have access requirements.

cards.title: Find Henry Moore’s Oval with Points
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Main campus sculpture walk
cards.notes: Approach the bronze from more than one angle and notice its surface texture; keep the visit to normal outdoor pathways and respect the artwork.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus sculpture with an official collection record.
cards.evidence_claim: Henry Moore’s Oval with Points is a 1969–70 bronze sculpture in Princeton’s campus collection.
cards.source_title: Oval with Points | Princeton University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus artwork; follow campus access guidance and do not climb on or handle the sculpture.

cards.title: See Nevelson’s changing steel forms
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Between Nassau Street and Firestone Library
cards.notes: Circle the sculpture slowly to notice how light and shadow change its cut-steel geometry, then use the Museum record for context.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Nevelson work positioned near Nassau Street and Firestone.
cards.evidence_claim: Atmosphere and Environment X is Louise Nevelson’s 1969–70 Cor-Ten steel sculpture, commissioned by Princeton University.
cards.source_title: Atmosphere and Environment X | Princeton University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus artwork; view from public paths and follow campus visitor guidance.

cards.title: Pause at Scott Burton’s Public Table
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Main campus
cards.notes: Use the collection record to understand the work’s functional-art idea, then pause briefly before continuing the campus art walk.
cards.short_summary: A campus artwork designed around social use.
cards.evidence_claim: Scott Burton’s Public Table is a 1978–79 cast-concrete sculpture on view in Princeton’s campus collection.
cards.source_title: Public Table | Princeton University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus artwork; use respectfully and follow any posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Take a garden reset at Prospect
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Prospect House grounds
cards.notes: Walk the garden paths at an unhurried pace and keep to the posted restrictions so the floral displays remain available for other visitors.
cards.short_summary: A garden stop on the Prospect House grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Prospect Gardens’ floral display is maintained for the University community and campus visitors to enjoy.
cards.access_notes: Observe the Gardens’ posted use restrictions and current campus visitor policy.

cards.title: Use TigerTransit for the final campus connection
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Princeton campus routes
cards.notes: Check the live route information before boarding and use the shuttle to connect campus stops instead of adding an unnecessary long walk.
cards.short_summary: A free campus shuttle option for visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: TigerTransit is free for all visitors and provides transportation around Princeton’s campus.
cards.source_title: Directions & Parking | Princeton University Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Check current routes and live tracking before travel; the Art Museum notes that TigerTransit does not stop directly at the Museum.
